 JUDGMENT

This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on account of the death of Sri Bharath S.B., in the road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is as follows:
On 13-04-2023 at about 12.20 p.m., the deceased was proceeding by riding the motor cycle bearing No. KA-68-L-4866 on Mysore-Benglauru Highway service road, near Challaghatta cross, Kengeri Hobli, at that time the driver of Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09- C-8258 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner came from Mysore side and suddenly changed the lane to left side from right side without applying any indicators or signal and thereby dashed against the said motorcycle and caused the accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately the deceased was shifted to Rajarajeshwari Hospital, but the said Bharath S.B. succumbed to the fatal injuries on the way to the Hospital.
Thereafter the postmortem was conducted in the said hospital and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 22 years and was Factory worker/student and earning Rs.20,000/ per month and he was contributing his entire income for the maintenance of his family.
Due to untimely death of deceased the petitioners have suffered mentally and physically and also the petitioners have lost the bread earner.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending lorry are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest to the petitioners.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and filed separate written statements.

Madhu G.C vs Cheluvaraju R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74412760/
2
The respondent No.1-owner of the offending lorry had filed written statement by denying all the averments of the petition.

This respondent has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the said lorry and contended that the deceased himself rode the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and dashed against his lorry.

The respondent No.1 has stated that the driver of the said Lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had valid driving licence and the vehicle also had valid insurance,
hence the 2 nd respondent is liable to pay the compensation.
Further this respondent has denied the age occupation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence the respondent No.1 owner prays to dismiss the petition against him.

The respondent No.2-insurer has filed written statement by admitting the issuance of Commerical vehicle package policy to the Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 and the liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has contended non-compliance of Sec.134(c), 147, 149, 158(6) of MV Act.

Further denied the cause and manner of accident and also further contended that at the time of accident the driver of the offending lorry as well as deceased were not holding valid and effective driving licence so also the insured lorry had no fitness certificate at the time of accident.
It has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the insured lorry, on the other hand, it has contended that the deceased is solely responsible in causing the accident.
Further this respondent has denied the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence the respondent No.2 insurance company prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Bharath S.B. S/o Shivayogi C. Banakar sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA- 09-C-8258 dated 13.04.2023 at about 12.20 p.m. and succumbed to injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and earnings of the deceased as stated in the claim petition?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Bharath S.B. S/o Shivayogi C. Banakar ?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
5. What order or award?
5.
In order to prove the claim petition, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15.

The respondent No.2 insurance company examined its official as RW1, IO as RW2 and its legal executive as RW.3 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.R.1 to R.4.

The petitioners to prove their claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
seizure mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, inquest report, PM report, head of charge sheet and IMV notice and reply, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 11.
9.
As per the documents, Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on the basis of the Ex.P.2 complaint given by one Kishan S.A. who is the friend of the deceased and also an eyewitness to the accident.
After the registration of FIR the IO conducted the spot mahazar, seizure mahazar and spot sketch as per Ex.P3 to P.5.
As per the spot mahazar and sketch marked at Ex.P3 & P.5 the accident spot is in the left side portion of the road in which the deceased was proceeding.
The photographs appended in the Ex.P.3 mahazar also shows that the driver of the offending lorry caused the accident while taking the right turn and entering into opposite lane.

10. The Ex.P.6 IMV report shows that the motorcycle of the deceased has got damages in its front number plate, front crash guard at the left side scratched, rear left side pillion rider hand gripper and foot rest scratched, front left side rear view mirror scratched.
On the other hand, the offending has got damages in its front bumper at right side scratched.
Thus, it is found that as per Ex.P3 mahazar P.5 sketch and Ex.P.6, the offending lorry has came to the opposite lane and caused the accident.

Even though the respondent No.1 denied the negligence of his driver, no evidence is placed by the respondent No.1 by examining the said driver and thereby establish that he has taken the turn after giving prior indications.
The Ex.P.3 to 5 evidentiates that the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 was negligent and caused the accident.

If, the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA_09-C- 8258 was not negligent and took turn after giving prior indications the said accident was not going to be caused and the right side bumper of the lorry was not going to be damaged.
This shows the gross negligence by the driver of the lorry.

Thereby the Ex.P3 to 5 mahazar, sketch and IMV report helped the petitioners to prove the alleged negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA_09-C- 8258.
11.
The respondent No.1 owner of the lorry bearing No.KA_09-C-8258 even though appeared before the tribunal but not produced any evidence or documents in support of his case.
The respondent No.2 filed written by denying the negligence on the part of the offending lorry and also examined its official as RW1 who has no personal knowledge about the accident.
12. Ex.P7 is the inquest and Ex.P8 is the postmortem report where both these documents discloses that the deceased succumbed due to crush injury to the head in the said accident.

13. It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: 14. In view of the ratio laid down in the authorities referred to above and applying the settled principle of law to the case at hand, which is further supported by the oral and documentary evidence adduced by PW-1, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident leading to this case indeed occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.KA_09-C-8258 resulting in deceased sustaining injuries.
15. Ex.P9 is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.KA_09-C-8258 for the offence punishable under Sec. 279, 337 & 304 (A) of IPC.
The investigating officer as per Ex.P9 charge sheet opined that the driver of offending lorry bearing No.KA_09-C-8258 driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
No other evidence is placed by the respondents to show the contributory negligence by the deceased.
During the course of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited so as to disprove the case of the petitioners.
16. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.

Looking to the oral as well as documentary evidence of the petitioners there are sufficient materials to show that Bharath S.B. died in the accident dated 13-04-2023 which is caused by the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA_09-C-8258.
Accordingly issue No.1 answered in the affirmative.
ISSUE NO.3 17.

As held herein above, the petitioners have proved that Bharath S.B. died on 13-04-2023 due to the injuries sustained in RTA, which is caused by driver of the offending lorry owned by respondent No.1.
18.
As contended in the petition the petitioners are the parents and sister of the deceased Bharath S.B.
The respondents do not specifically deny the relationship of petitioner with deceased.
The petitioners to prove their relationship with the deceased, have produced the notarized copies of Aadhar cards of petitioners along with deceased which are marked under Ex.P12 to P.15.
During the course of recording the evidence the notarized copies of Aadhaar cards are compared with the original documents and found correct.
19. The respondents do not dispute the Aadhaar cards produced by the petitioners.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence to disprove the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

20. In the absence of contradictory evidence the evidence of the petitioners to be accepted and it is considered that, petitioners are the parents and sister of deceased being the dependents are entitled for compensation.
Accordingly Issue No.3 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text:
The issue No.1 & 3 are answered in the affirmative by holding that the deceased Bharath S.B.
died in the RTA dated 13-04-2023 caused by the negligent driving by the driver of Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 and the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.
22.
Now the quantum of compensation is to be decided.
In the Aadhaar card of the deceased Bharath S.B. are produced at Ex.P12, the date of birth of the deceased is shown as 02.02.2000.
The accident took place on 13.04.2023.
If it is considered, as on the date of the accident the age of the deceased was 23 years.
23. As stated in the petition deceased was a Factory worker and also mechanical Engineering Student and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But no such documents are produced to show the occupation and income of the deceased and also to show that the deceased was a Mechanical Engineering Student.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased be considered to Rs.16,000/- per month.
24. As per Sarala varma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 18.

Since the deceased is a bachelor 50% of the income is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, then the total loss of dependency would be Rs.17,28,000/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 18 = Rs.34,56,000/- minus half of the income i.e., (Rs.34,56,000 /- - Rs.17,28,000/-) = Rs.17,28,000/-).

25. In Civil Special leave petition (Civil No.25590/2014 dated 31.10.2016 (National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "While determining the income, in case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."
26. As per the above decisions 40% out of loss of dependency has to be granted towards future prospects which would Rs.6,91,200/-.
27. The Petitioners are the parents and sister of the deceased.

Therefore they are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,000/- each (Rs.40,000/x 10% hike every three years from 2017 as per Pranay Sethi Case)
under the head of loss of consortium.

28. Further I inclined to award Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses (this amount is calculated as per Pranaya Sethi case with enhanced rate at 10% after three years).

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1. Loss of dependency Rs. 17,28,000/-

29. Liability:-
In the petition it is alleged that the respondent No.1& 2 are the owner and insurer of the Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258.
The respondent No.1 insurance company in its written statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle by the respondent No.2.
The respondent No.2 insurance company in its objection statement has admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle.
30. The respondent No.2-insurance company in respect of liability has taken two specific defence.
Firstly it contends that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C- 8258 was not having valid permit to ply on the road.
Secondly the driver of the said offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 was not having valid driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident.
By contending the said two violations, the respondent No.2 insurance company examined two witnesses in support of their defence.
It is the burden on the respondent No.2 insurance company to show the violation of the policy conditions by the respondent No.1 owner.

31. To discharge its burden the respondent No.2- insurance company examined its official as RW1 who deposed about the non-existence of permit for the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 at the time of accident.

Further the respondent No.2 also examined the IO who also deposed that in his investigation he has found that the said offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C- 8258 had no permit at the time of accident.

In this regard in combined with the oral evidence of RW1 and 2 if we see the Ex.P.9 charge sheet, it shows that the IO has found that the said offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had no valid permit to ply on the road, as such he has invoked Sec.187 and 192A of IMV Act.
The respondent No.1 owner who also appeared in this case and also cross- examined the RW1 and 2 failed to establish that the said vehicle had the valid permit at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 who appeared and cross-examined the witnesses failed to produce the permit by showing the contrary to the contents of Ex.P.9 charge sheet.
If the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had valid permit the same could be produced by the respondent No.1.
In spite of sufficient opportunity the respondent No.1 owner not adduced any evidence by establishing the existence of permit.
Thereby, the respondent No.2 successfully discharged its burden by establishing that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had no permit at the time of accident.
32. Coming to the next defence the respondent No.2 insurance company contends that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid driving licence at the time of accident.

But on perusal of Madhu G.C vs Cheluvaraju R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74412760/
8 Ex.P.9 charge sheet the investigation officer not invoked any penal sections against the driver and owner for driving and allowing to drive without driving licence.
The investigation officer who examined before this court as RW2 also produced the true copy of the driving licence as Ex.R.1.
as per the said Ex.R.1 the driver of the offending vehicle had valid driving licence of non-transporting vehicle till 23-03- 2035 and transporting vehicle till 20-03-2023.
The date of accident was 13-04-2023.

But the respondent No.2 insurance company filed IA No.VII and took summons to the RTO, PVD Kolkata, West Bengal State to furnish the driving licence details of the accused by name Ramesh Kumar S/o Dhiran Singh, in Driving Licence No.WB0120151012450.
When the details of Ex.R.1 was sent under IA No.Vii to rto, pvd kolkata, west bengal state, they replied in their letter dated 04-12-2024 by saying that "THIS DRIVING LICENCE NUMBER NOT EXIST".

Thereby the official communication made by the office of the Director, Transport Directorate, Kolkata Zone,
there is no driving licence under the Driving Licence No.WB0120151012450.

Thereby the said communication establishes that the said Ramesh Kumar S/o Dhiran Singh who was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident had no driving licence and the Ex.R.1 which is copy of driving licence is a fake and fabricated one.
Thereby it is established before this tribunal that the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving licence at the time of accident.
33. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is actively involved in the trial of this petition who cross-examined PW1, RW1 and 2.
The respondent No.1 being the owner not made out any grounds to reject the defence of the respondent No.2 - insurance company.

The document and report sent by Director, Transport Directorate, Kolkata Zone, being the public document clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid driving licence for the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258.
34.

The respondent No.2 insurance company has taken specific defence of non existence of permit to the offending vehicle and no driving licence to the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.
KA-09-C-8258 and also taken steps to prove the said contentions.

Further in the copy of charge sheet which is available in the file shows that Sec. 192 of IMV Act is invoked by alleging the non- existing of the permit to the offending vehicle at the time of accident.

35. The charge sheet as well as the evidence of RW1 and 2 clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A- 6268 at the time of accident and also driving licence to the driver.
The respondent No.1 -owner who appeared and participated in the trial, has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle and driving licence to the driver.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
36. By keeping the arguments canvassed by both the parties in background, there is no dispute that at the time of accident the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-09- C-8258 was covered with insurance.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established as there was no permit for the offending vehicle and no DL for the driver at the time of accident.

37. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258 even after appearing and contesting the case has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.

Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the offending Madhu G.C vs Cheluvaraju R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74412760/
9 vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258 to ply on the road without permit and the driver to drive the same without driving licence is a breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.
Hence, the respondent No.1 owner is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The petitioners are entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, the Issue No.2 answered in the Partly affirmative and Issue No.4 answered in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.5:-
38.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.25,96,200/-
(Rupees Twenty five lakhs ninety six thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1- owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The case against the respondent No.2- insurance company stands dismissed.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:40:20.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and 2 on their proper identification and remaining 25% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in their names.
By considering the quantum of compensation awarded to petitioner No.3 it is directed to release the entire share of the petitioner No.3 on her proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

4. On the basis of the rival contentions, the following issues were framed by this court:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Bharath S.B. S/o Shivayogi C. Banakar sustained injuries due to rash and negligent act of driving of Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA- 09-C-8258 dated 13.04.2023 at about 12.20 p.m. and succumbed to injuries?

3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Bharath S.B. S/o Shivayogi C. Banakar ?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
5. What order or award?

The issue No.1 & 3 are answered in the affirmative by holding that the deceased Bharath S.B.
died in the RTA dated 13-04-2023 caused by the negligent driving by the driver of Cement Mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 and the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
As contended in the petition the petitioners are the parents and sister of the deceased Bharath S.B.

16. As per well settled position of law the standard of proof in claim petition like present one, is only preponderance of probabilities.
The respondent No.1 owner who also appeared in this case and also cross- examined the RW1 and 2 failed to establish that the said vehicle had the valid permit at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 who appeared and cross-examined the witnesses failed to produce the permit by showing the contrary to the contents of Ex.P.9 charge sheet.
If the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had valid permit the same could be produced by the respondent No.1.
In spite of sufficient opportunity the respondent No.1 owner not adduced any evidence by establishing the existence of permit.
Thereby, the respondent No.2 successfully discharged its burden by establishing that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-09-C-8258 had no permit at the time of accident.
Thereby the official communication made by the office of the Director, Transport Directorate, Kolkata Zone,
there is no driving licence under the Driving Licence No.WB0120151012450.
Thereby it is established before this tribunal that the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving licence at the time of accident.
The document and report sent by Director, Transport Directorate, Kolkata Zone, being the public document clearly establishes that as on the date of accident, there was no valid driving licence for the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258.
34.
35. The charge sheet as well as the evidence of RW1 and 2 clearly set out the aspect regarding non existence of the permit for the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-53-A- 6268 at the time of accident and also driving licence to the driver.
The respondent No.1 -owner who appeared and participated in the trial, has not adduced any evidence by showing the existence of permit to the offending vehicle and driving licence to the driver.
Hence, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
But the violation of the condition of insurance policy is stands established as there was no permit for the offending vehicle and no DL for the driver at the time of accident.
37. In this case, the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258 even after appearing and contesting the case has not lead any evidence to show that he has not violated the policy condition willfully.
Thereby the conduct of respondent No.1 -owner allowing the offending Madhu G.C vs Cheluvaraju R on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74412760/
9 vehicle bearing No. KA-09-C-8258 to ply on the road without permit and the driver to drive the same without driving licence is a breach of policy condition and thereby the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability.
The respondent No.1 being the owner cannot take the benefit of his own wrong.
Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recover when there is clear breach of rules of IMV Act and liability to pay compensation is on the respondent No.1 owner.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.25,96,200/-
(Rupees Twenty five lakhs ninety six thousand two hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1- owner is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
The case against the respondent No.2- insurance company stands dismissed.
The petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 40:40:20.
Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner No.1 and 2, 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner No.1 and 2 on their proper identification and remaining 25% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in their names.
By considering the quantum of compensation awarded to petitioner No.3 it is directed to release the entire share of the petitioner No.3 on her proper identification.
